lead: A PHP file is only text until a web server hands it to a PHP interpreter. A Java servlet needs a container that starts it and calls it for each request. XAMPP is a free package that puts Apache, PHP, MySQL or MariaDB and Perl on one laptop, with a control panel to start and stop them. Developers use it to run and test code on localhost before uploading to a hosted server. Some syllabi call this environment setup.
prereq: You need: Unit 1's client-server and web-server ideas, and 4.1 for what a .php file contains.

sections.h3: XAMPP: one package for a laptop

blocks.text: XAMPP installs four parts: Apache is the web server, MySQL or MariaDB is the database, PHP is the server-side language, and Perl is included for older scripts. The control panel is a small program that starts and stops Apache and MySQL; it is not itself a web server. A green label means the service is running. The control panel also shows the Apache and PHP version numbers. On Windows the usual install folder is C:/xampp.

The document root is the folder whose files Apache serves. In XAMPP it is htdocs, so C:/xampp/htdocs/shop/pay.php is requested as http://localhost/shop/pay.php. The folder shop becomes part of the URL path. MySQL listens on port 3306 by default, and PHP connects to it with an extension such as mysqli or PDO.

Two text files control the setup. php.ini holds PHP settings: error display, upload size, and which extensions load. httpd.conf holds Apache settings: the port in a Listen line, the DocumentRoot, and module loading. After editing either file, restart the service from the control panel.

sections.h3: Apache: ports, modules and virtual hosts

blocks.text: Apache is an HTTP server. It listens on a port: 80 for http and 443 for https with TLS. A URL path is mapped under the document root; static files are sent directly, while a .php request is passed to PHP. Apache can run PHP as a module inside its own process, or send the request to a separate FastCGI process. XAMPP usually loads the module; IIS uses FastCGI.
A module is an optional feature loaded at start. mod_ssl adds HTTPS, mod_rewrite rewrites URLs, and mod_proxy forwards requests. Each has a LoadModule line in httpd.conf.

A virtual host lets one Apache serve several site names on the same IP and port. The browser sends a Host header, and Apache picks the matching VirtualHost block with its ServerName and DocumentRoot. localhost is a name for the loopback address 127.0.0.1; the hosts file resolves it before DNS. Only one program can listen on a given address and port. If another program already uses 80, Apache fails to start. Change Listen 80 to another port in httpd.conf, or stop the other program. A non-default port must appear in the URL, as in http://localhost:8080/.

sections.h3: Tomcat for servlets, IIS for Windows PHP

blocks.text: Tomcat is a servlet container and JSP engine. It runs Java servlets and JSP pages; it does not run PHP. Its default connector port is 8080. The webapps folder is where web applications live. A folder shop with a WEB-INF folder is a web application, reached at http://localhost:8080/shop/. A WAR file is a zipped web application: copy shop.war into webapps, and Tomcat unpacks it on start. The connector port is set in server.xml.

IIS is Microsoft's web server for Windows. It listens on port 80 by default. It does not run PHP natively; install PHP and add a FastCGI handler that runs php-cgi.exe. IIS organises sites with bindings and application pools. A site whose root is the project folder can serve http://localhost/pay.php.

Port conflicts are the common failure. Apache and IIS both default to 80, so they cannot both use the same address and port. Tomcat uses 8080, and MySQL uses 3306. Use netstat to see which program holds a port. The hosts file, at C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts on Windows or /etc/hosts on Linux and macOS, maps names such as localhost to 127.0.0.1.

figure.caption: The worked example: Apache on port 80 serves C:/xampp/htdocs/shop/pay.php as http://localhost/shop/pay.php, and Tomcat on port 8080 serves shop.war as http://localhost:8080/shop/. Apache and IIS both default to port 80, so the dashed IIS path can run only when port 80 is free.

spec.title: Ports and paths
spec.aria: A browser branches to Apache on port 80 with a PHP module and MySQL 3306, to Tomcat on port 8080 with servlets and JSP, and to IIS on port 80 with PHP FastCGI; the IIS path is dashed because port 80 can host only one server.

examples.question: A Windows laptop runs XAMPP at C:/xampp. The file C:/xampp/htdocs/shop/pay.php must be opened in a browser, and a shop.war is deployed to Tomcat. Give the two URLs and their ports. Port 80 is already used by another program: what do you change?
steps: XAMPP's document root is C:/xampp/htdocs. The file lies in the shop folder under it, so its URL path is /shop/pay.php. Apache listens on port 80 by default, and 80 is the default for http, so no port is written: http://localhost/shop/pay.php.

Tomcat listens on port 8080 by default. A file shop.war in webapps becomes the context /shop, so the servlet URL is http://localhost:8080/shop/. The port 8080 must be written because it is not the default for http.

If port 80 is taken, Apache cannot bind to it. Stop the other program, or change Listen 80 to another free port in httpd.conf. If Apache takes 8080, Tomcat must move its connector to a different free port in server.xml, because two programs cannot share one port.
examples.answer: The PHP page is http://localhost/shop/pay.php on port 80; the servlet application is http://localhost:8080/shop/ on port 8080.

traps: Calling Tomcat a PHP server: Tomcat runs servlets and JSP, not .php files.
Putting PHP files in Tomcat's webapps folder: XAMPP serves PHP from htdocs.
Mixing up php.ini and httpd.conf: the first sets PHP options, the second sets Apache's port and document root.
Thinking localhost is a folder: it is a hostname for 127.0.0.1, resolved through the hosts file.
Changing Listen 80 in httpd.conf and expecting Tomcat's 8080 port to move too; the Tomcat connector is set in server.xml.

quiz.q: What does the X in XAMPP stand for, and which four main parts does XAMPP install?
quiz.a: Cross-platform; Apache, MySQL or MariaDB, PHP and Perl.

quiz.q: Why can Apache and IIS not both listen on port 80 on the same machine address?
quiz.a: A TCP port on one address accepts one listening program; the second bind fails.

quiz.q: XAMPP is installed at C:/xampp. A file is C:/xampp/htdocs/blog/post.php. Give its URL on default Apache.
A file shop.war is copied to Tomcat's webapps folder. Give the default URL of the application context.
Apache is changed to Listen 8080, but Tomcat still uses 8080. What happens, and what is a correct fix?
quiz.a: Apache or Tomcat fails to bind because both want 8080. Change Tomcat's Connector port in server.xml to a free port, or put Apache back on 80.

quiz.q: Which file sets PHP's upload limit, and which file sets Apache's Listen port?
quiz.a: php.ini sets PHP's upload limit; httpd.conf sets Apache's Listen port.

quiz.q: A student puts pay.php in Tomcat's webapps/shop. Why does the browser show the PHP source or an error?
quiz.a: Tomcat is a servlet container and does not run PHP. Put the file under XAMPP htdocs or configure IIS with FastCGI.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production teams rarely install XAMPP on a server; they build images that contain a web server, PHP-FPM and the application, then run them with Docker Compose or Kubernetes. Apache or IIS often sits behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and forwards requests to several application containers. Search for php-fpm, nginx reverse proxy, Tomcat Catalina, IIS FastCGI and Docker Compose to see the same ideas at scale.
